note: Registered E2E suites with no assertion about a 401 or 403. Seeded from the state on 2026-08-15 so the gate can only ratchet down. The `sha` pins the reason to the file it was written about: EDIT THE SUITE AND ITS EXEMPTION EXPIRES, because the person editing it is the one person who has the context to add the missing case. Re-stamping the sha without adding a denial is available and is a decision someone has to write down.

test/e2e-oauth-login.ts.reason: REVIEWED 2026-09-04 — in the standard test config no provider is configured, so every authorize and callback answers 503 before any principal question can be reached. That is the suite's purpose against a running node: prove the routes are MOUNTED and gated rather than 404, which is the failure a mounting mistake produces and which no unit test can see. The refusals that involve an identity — an unmapped subject, a state that does not match, a session issued to the wrong account — need a working IdP and are covered by test/unit/oauth-login.test.ts against a fake one.

test/e2e-portfolio-origin.ts.reason: REVIEWED 2026-09-04 — the portfolio origin is a public vanity host: <username>.portfolio.<apex> serves whatever that owner chose to publish, to anyone, with no session anywhere in the flow. The suite self-spawns a node with the origin provisioned because the shared runner keeps the flag off. Its refusals are host-shaped and asserted four times over, all as the same 404: an account that has not published yet, a username no account holds, a reserved label ('www'), and an owner who set enabled:false. One answer for all four, so the host cannot be used to find out which usernames exist. There is no door here for a second principal to be refused at.

test/e2e-mcp-sse-parity.ts.reason: REVIEWED 2026-09-04 — the question this suite asks has no refusal in it: does a change an agent makes reach an open page on the right SSE domain, and does a change on one domain stay off another (a memory write must not announce itself as a board change). Both halves are about routing, and both are asserted for one owner. WHAT WOULD BE WORTH ADDING, and is not a denial in the 401/403 sense either: a SECOND owner holding an open stream must not hear the first owner's change at all — an SSE event that crossed owners would leak that someone is working and roughly on what, which no other suite in this repo currently asks. Left as a note here rather than filed, because it needs a second live stream and that machinery does not exist in this file yet.

test/e2e-pacing.ts.reason: REVIEWED 2026-09-04 — the refusal is the whole subject and it is 402. The suite self-spawns a node with AIMEAT_PACING_TOLL_DEFAULT set and proves the hole the developer spotted: a MONEY-priced capability used to pass the pacing floor untouched, so paying removed the rate bound instead of adding to it. What it asserts is that a caller out of pace is refused with 402 whatever the call is paid in. Pace belongs to the human in whose name the caller acts, so a second principal of the same owner shares one balance by design and would be refused identically. The interesting second principal is another OWNER, whose pace is a different balance, and that is where a morsel MOVES rather than where it runs out: test/e2e-ext-paywall.ts holds it, asserting that a cross-owner payment is an atomic debit-caller + credit-owner while an anti-abuse toll burns without crediting anyone.

test/e2e-exchange-projection.ts.reason: REVIEWED 2026-09-04 — the cross-owner refusal is here and it is the point of the suite; it is a PAYWALL, so it answers 402 rather than 403. 'BYPASS: calling the backing extension action directly is NOT free once a tool sells it' registers a stranger, calls the extension behind a priced listing as that stranger, and asserts 402 PAYMENT_REQUIRED naming every product that sells the capability — the hole measured on production on 2026-07-27, where any signed-in principal could POST the extension action and get the paid answer for nothing. Its control is the next test: the provider still calls their own extension free. 402 is the correct code for a door that refuses because the caller has not paid rather than because they may not; the detector counts 401 and 403.

test/e2e-registration-invites.ts.reason: REVIEWED 2026-09-04. This surface has no refusal to test, and that is the design rather than an omission. The suite guards ONE route, POST /v1/registration-invites, which is open by necessity: an AI calls it with a person's email before that person has any account, so there is no principal to refuse. Its whole security property is the OPPOSITE of a refusal — the response must be byte-identical whether the address is new, already has an account, or already has a live invitation, because any difference turns it into an address-checking machine. The suite asserts exactly that in three tests, plus the per-address cap and single-use expiry that bound the abuse a 403 cannot. There is no second route on this router: no listing, no read, nothing an owner could reach across. A 401 or 403 added here would have to be invented.

test/e2e-mcp-scopes.ts.reason: Reviewed 2026-08-15. This suite is ALL refusal, and none of it is status-shaped: the MCP tool surface refuses by not registering the tool (assert(!tools.includes(...))) and a filtered call comes back through a local {ok} wrapper rather than isError. Kept exempt because the detector cannot see those two shapes, not because the fence is untested — it now also asserts that a '*' agent is refused every tool riding a SCOPES_OUTSIDE_WILDCARD word, list derived from the vocabulary.

test/e2e-mcp-v2.ts.reason: REVIEWED 2026-08-16 (E2E test-quality audit, finding e2e-mcp-v2:92). This surface does not refuse with a status code: a tool outside the caller's surface or scopes is never REGISTERED on the session, so the refusal is an ABSENCE from tools/list — src/mcp/index.ts calls it a hard skip, silent, not a scope denial. The suite now drives that refusal with a second agent holding only memory:read, asserting its agent-surface listing is a strict subset with no memory_write while the broad agent keeps it. There is no 401 or 403 on this door to assert.

test/e2e-x402-testnet.ts.reason: REVIEWED 2026-09-04. This suite never runs in CI and has no refusal to add. Its first twelve lines are a skip guard: it exits 0 unless AIMEAT_X402_ENABLED=true AND the REAL x402.org facilitator is in use, because Phase B signs an EIP-3009 authorization with a throwaway key and settles ~0.10 USDC on Base Sepolia. It is a manual on-chain acceptance harness a person runs after funding an address, not a suite. Adding a cross-owner case here would write a test that never executes, which is worse than the gap: it reads as coverage. The refusals on the same surface that DO run belong in e2e-money-audit, which is in the guard tier. If this suite is ever made to run unattended, this line expires with its sha.

test/e2e-organism-member-visibility.ts.reason: Reviewed 2026-08-16. This suite is entirely about refusal, and none of it is a status: the roster doors answer 200 with the roster REDACTED (members_hidden, an empty members[], empty agentGaiis), because hiding who is in an organism is not the same as hiding that it exists. It asserts that on BOTH doors — the members listing and the detail handler, which is a separate handler with its own canSeeMembers call. Re-seeded 2026-08-23 after adding test 8 (a duplicated ?member= param must not 500 the list, CodeQL type-confusion) — a correctness assertion, not a new gated surface, so the exemption still holds.

test/e2e-connect-tunnel-delivery.ts.reason: REVIEWED 2026-09-04 — one owner, one agent, and that is the subject rather than an omission: the suite measures the DELIVERY invariants of the push tunnel (latency budget, id-dedup, no-loss across a disconnect, that an ack is not a completion, that a status change is what clears the backlog, that an offline agent gets backlog and not live). Each of those is a statement about one agent's own queue, and a second principal cannot make any of them truer. The access half of the same transport — who may subscribe to what, and what a revoked token can still open — is test/e2e-connect-tunnel-records.ts, which asserts it three ways against a second owner.

test/e2e-connect-tunnel-records.ts.reason: REVIEWED 2026-09-04 — this suite is denser in refusals than most suites the gate passes; it just does not speak HTTP. Its refusals arrive as tunnel frames: test 5 subscribes B's agent to A's PRIVATE workspace and asserts the ack carries 0 accepted and rejected[0].reason === 'access_denied'; test 6 then writes a record and asserts NO push reaches B (push access is REST read access, which is the security invariant the file header states); test 7b revokes A's agent token and asserts a new tunnel cannot be opened with it at all. Those are three cross-principal denials on a transport with no status line. This is the same blind spot the detector already learned once for MCP's isError — the file header records it saying e2e-mcp-cross-owner.ts, a file that exists solely to refuse owner B seventeen ways, had no denial case. Adding an HTTP call to this suite purely so the scanner can see something would be a worse test than the three it already has.

test/e2e-audio-speech.ts.reason: REVIEWED 2026-09-04. The whole surface is GET /v1/libs/aimeat-audio.js, /aimeat-speech.js and the /v1/libs index — served browser libraries, and serving them to anybody is the requirement rather than an oversight: an app running in a visitor's browser loads them by URL before that visitor has any account, and routes/libs.ts registers them with no auth middleware for exactly that reason. A 401 here would break every published app. What COULD go wrong on this surface is the file being stale or wrong, which check:sdk and check:vendored already gate, not who may read it.

test/e2e-message-transcript.ts.reason: REVIEWED 2026-08-16 (E2E test-quality audit, finding e2e-message-transcript:145). This surface refuses with 404, not 403, and that is deliberate: the transcribe route looks the message up as storage.getDirectMessage(id, ownerGhii), so a caller who is not a party to the message is told the message does not exist rather than that it exists and is not theirs. The suite now drives that refusal with a THIRD owner, on the plain and the force:true paths, and reads the sender's copy back afterwards to show nothing was written; the recipient reaching their OWN copy is the positive control. There is no 401 or 403 on this route to assert.

test/e2e-members.ts.reason: REVIEWED 2026-09-04 — GET /v1/portfolio/members is a public list with no authenticated door on it, so 'what does a second principal get' has one answer: the same list. Its only refusal is content-shaped and IS asserted — test 2 publishes nothing for one of the four owners and asserts that owner is absent, and test 5 resolves every listed member back to a published portfolio, so the list cannot name somebody who did not opt in. The four owners exist to cover the four gaii shapes a portfolio config can be stored under, not to compare principals.

test/e2e-attachment-sweep.ts.reason: REVIEWED 2026-09-04. There is no door here to refuse. This suite is IN-PROCESS: it imports createServer, loadConfig and sweepReferenceAttachments directly and calls the sweep function, and it makes zero fetch() calls (measured: 0). What it tests is a background job deciding whether an attachment reference is retried or expired, which has no caller and therefore no principal to refuse. The HTTP doors that create those attachments live in the DM suites and carry their refusals there. If this ever grows an HTTP call, the sha pin expires with it.

test/e2e-agent-connect-email.ts.reason: REVIEWED 2026-09-04 — there is no second principal, because there is no first one. Every test here drives POST /v1/agents/device-authorize, which is unauthenticated by construction: RFC 8628's whole point is that the credential being collected is the caller's first, so a session gate is impossible (the same reasoning carries the route-scope exemption for its ecosystem twin). The door's entire refusal vocabulary IS asserted: 404 NO_ACCOUNT for an email no account holds, 400 INVALID_EMAIL for one that is not an address, and the one-verified-email-per-account invariant the resolver depends on — without which an email would resolve to two accounts and the caller could not tell which one they had connected to. The 404 is a deliberate existence answer, not a leak: a person who typed their address wrong has to be able to find that out. The cross-owner question this door raises — can I start a connection to somebody ELSE's account by naming their email — is decided one step later at approval, and test/e2e-app-agent-deploy.ts asserts it ('CROSS-OWNER authenticated device-authorize stays pending (never auto-approved)').

test/e2e-public-activity.ts.reason: REVIEWED 2026-09-04 — GET /v1/public/activity-feed is public by definition, and every refusal it has is content-shaped rather than principal-shaped. All of them are asserted: a PRIVATE organism does not appear, a knowledge package without catalog_listed does not appear, nothing owned by system@ reaches the ticker, and the seeded built-in skills specifically do not. Those four are the security property this feed has — an action becomes visible because it was made public, not because of who is asking — and asking as a second principal would return the identical feed.

test/e2e-public-totals.ts.reason: REVIEWED 2026-09-04. GET /v1/public/node-totals has no refusal to test and that is the requirement rather than an omission: it powers the landing panel a visitor sees before they have an account, and the suite asserts it answers with no Authorization header at all. The question a public counter DOES raise is asked instead, and it is not status-shaped: a counter that rises when a PRIVATE organism is created tells an anonymous caller that one exists, which is the whole of what private was supposed to prevent. Added 2026-09-04 and it holds. If an authenticated door is ever added to this router, this line expires with its sha.

test/e2e-datapackage-odata.ts.reason: REVIEWED 2026-08-15: this surface has no refusal to test, and that is the design rather than an omission. An OData feed serves the rows of a PUBLISHED data package, whose CSV already sits at a permanent, world-readable /v1/pub address; putting a token in front of the feed while the file stays open would be theatre, not a control. There is therefore no second principal that gets a different answer. What the suite DOES prove instead is the fence that exists here: test 13b shows the feed is a door onto packages and cannot be steered at the owner's other storage, and tests 7-11 prove every unimplemented query construct is REFUSED (501/400) rather than ignored — which on this surface is the failure with real consequences, because an ignored $filter returns the wrong rows into somebody's report with no symptom. If the metered feed is ever built it will be a separate authenticated door, and that one owes a 401/403 case.

test/e2e-mcp-install.ts.reason: Reviewed 2026-08-27, re-reviewed 2026-09-02 when the second door was added. The surface is TWO public GETs (/v1/connect/mcp.json and /v1/connect/install) that return a config file or a double-click script holding this node's MCP address and a name the caller picked. They read nothing owned by anybody, so there is no principal to refuse: 401 and 403 are not answers they can give, and asserting one would mean inventing a gate the feature does not have. Their only refusals are 400s for a client or desktop they do not know, which the suite asserts by code. The fence the doors DO have is tested instead, in 'The door tells a second principal nothing about the first': two registered owners and an unauthenticated caller must get byte-identical bytes, with neither owner's name in them. That is the failure worth catching here, because the day these routes start reflecting their caller, a door that takes no auth is handing one person's account to whoever asks next.
